conclusion: All 58 institutions have an overview and ten separate subject tab pages. The page structure is complete but factual coverage is uneven: 365 research gaps remain and 0 evidence-poor tabs defer search indexing while remaining readable. Ten Articles, six Blogs, two historical News stories and eight state collections are written. Local frontend and CMS payloads are prepared; no remote publication or CMS data import has occurred.

cautions: Reference rankings, traffic and conversion performance were not available; structure alone does not establish SEO success.
The initial course-and-fee audit used a different path from the actual course-fee navigation target; do not infer that the supplied fee tab itself was broken.
The sampled news route contained three H1 elements; our target is one main H1 with meaningful H2/H3 sections.
Approximate fees, financial-scheme eligibility and aggregate ratings require their own evidence; do not borrow those claims.

page_outline.title: Agriculture study at this institution
page_outline.intent: Identify the school/college and explain the relevant learning setting.

page_outline.title: Key facts at a glance
page_outline.intent: Location, ownership, affiliation and verified establishment details in a small table.

page_outline.title: Agriculture programmes, fees and eligibility
page_outline.intent: Programme table with duration, qualifying subjects, fee period, quota, source year and offering-detail links.

page_outline.title: How to apply and which route applies
page_outline.intent: Programme-specific entry route, documents and dated notices; distinguish university admissions from state/ICAR counselling.

page_outline.title: ICAR accreditation: course, unit and validity
page_outline.intent: Show the precise listed programme/unit and term; link to the official source and the accreditation explainer.

page_outline.title: Curriculum and practical learning
page_outline.intent: Verified subjects, farm/lab work, RAWE or experiential learning where the institution actually documents them.

page_outline.title: Campus, laboratories and student facilities
page_outline.intent: Authentic photos, useful captions and verified facilities, with location/campus scope.

page_outline.title: Scholarships and cost support
page_outline.intent: Applicable scheme, source year, conditions and exclusions; never assume every general scholarship covers agriculture.

page_outline.title: Career support and reported outcomes
page_outline.intent: Separate general career possibilities from programme-specific placement evidence; attach year and scope to figures.

page_outline.title: Other agriculture institutions to compare
page_outline.intent: Relevant alternatives by programme, location and verified facts; no unsupported ranking.

page_outline.title: Admission updates and useful guides
page_outline.intent: Relevant published news plus explanatory articles/blogs, automatically selected through CMS relations.

page_outline.title: Applicant questions answered
page_outline.intent: Institution-specific answers with useful contextual links, without repeating entire sections.

page_outline.title: Sources and content review date
page_outline.intent: Concise official references and a real editorial review date/byline; keep internal research gaps outside public marketing copy.

architecture: University profile links to its actual course offerings, relevant programme guides and a small contextual reading set.
Each guide links back to relevant institution profiles and the correct programme page.
News links to the affected institution/programme; the institution shows the same published update.
State collection pages connect relevant profiles where there is enough distinct useful information.

editorial_types.role: Evergreen explanatory guides backed by official sources.
editorial_types.example: How to check an agriculture programme’s ICAR term.

editorial_types.role: Decision support, comparison methods and practical applicant checklists.
editorial_types.example: Questions to ask before choosing an agriculture campus.
A specific official revised counselling notice; not a generic admissions-open headline.

editorial_types.role: Only a genuine attributed institutional announcement.
editorial_types.example: An actual sourced announcement, labelled by its publisher and date.

linking_rules: Use ordinary crawlable <a href> links with concise descriptive anchor text.
Link where the destination answers the reader’s next question; avoid repeated keyword anchors and unrelated footer link dumps.
Do not activate planned URLs until the destination is published and returns its real content.
Give the main hub a useful summary; create separate admission/fee pages only when each can answer a distinct query with enough unique verified information.
Keep one canonical address for each post and institution intent; no duplicated article/blog copies.
Do not publish blanket exam routes, loan-scheme eligibility or all-course ICAR claims.
cms_changes_needed: Implemented: structured university/editorial content fields with deterministic TOC and source references.
Implemented: university/programme editorial relations and published related-reading display.
Implemented: an honest Agrico Editorial byline and review date, separate from publication and official-notice dates.
Implemented: canonical editorial routes, local images and sitemap entries.
Prepared: slug-matched CMS content and media payloads. No CMS data import or remote deployment was executed.
google_guidance: Original useful analysis and institution-specific facts matter more than merely rewriting another publisher.
There is no Google-prescribed word-count target; depth follows the applicant question and available evidence.
Use meaningful links and a coherent hierarchy; links are not a guaranteed ranking formula.
FAQ answers remain useful for students, but Google retired FAQ rich results from 7 May 2026. Do not promise FAQ snippets.
Use accurate entity, breadcrumb and editorial structured data matching visible content; never invent AggregateRating.
Public crawlability, canonical URLs, sitemaps, mobile usability and Search Console verification are launch checks. No one can guarantee immediate first position.
